reading_rules.text: Stage 4 starts from the observations, not the verses (researcher, #2526 Q7, 2026-11-21): the subgroups and the stage 3 observations on them are the input, the behaviours are discovered from analysing them, and the base data is read back into only occasionally. Every finding of step 3.1 or 3.2 rests on named observations (a traced node on each, with an occurrence node as well) and its occurrence nodes lie within the occurrences those observations cover; an occurrence outside them is allowed only where the finding records a read-back (the verse and why). Each node has a role from reading.node_roles other than lexical, chosen by the reading. A 3.3 finding carries nodes on the occurrences of both sides in the shared verses.

A finding of a stage 4 row is checked by the rules of observationrecord.check and check_item_parts (kind, text, basis, route, parts.item and what the item needs, node roles, collection of each node) and by RG, RW and RS, which are not restated here: one observation for each finding, never a duplicate, with a node on each word it applies to (RO11, RW-03); founded in the observations and never a restatement of the verse (B:131); parts.item is one of the items the row's item uses (cfg_setting layer.reading). An observation whose nodes all bear on an act is refused: those words are nodes of the observation of the act. A finding is a building block of a behaviour and never a claim (stage 5).

Nothing the step reads is lost on the way to stage 5. Step 3.1: every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on by a finding or declared in not_used with its reason in words. Step 3.2: every 3.1 observation of the collection is gathered into a behaviour (a traced node on it from a flag finding of type discovery) or declared in not_gathered with its reason, and the row has at least one behaviour unless it is recorded as none with its reason. A behaviour names and gathers; it makes no claim about what the behaviour is.

An earlier inner-being observation with a node on the occurrences of a 3.1 row (any stage but lexical, layer-1, layer-2 and layer-3) is shown in the pull for information and may be actioned in `existing`: accepted, modified, deleted, merged or left, each with its reason, through observationrecord (RW-01, RW-09); nothing is demanded of it, and it counts for nothing in the check. A row answered again withdraws its earlier observations with the reason.
One observation per finding, never a duplicate description; a finding applying to several verses or words carries several nodes, each with the word's role in it.

Read outward from the verse, not inward from the scope's question. First record everything the verse carries, each with where it bears (chapter, thread, signpost); answer the scope's question last. A verse often has two or three significances, and none is dropped.
Read the verse in its passage and genre; name the speaker; explore figures for what they say about the inner being; take paired and opposite acts together. Restating a verse is not reading it.

Find the main inner-being operation, and give every word that bears on it its role in this finding (cfg_setting reading.node_roles): characteristic, qualifier and what it gives the characteristic, object or content, relational target, or enactment. A word read in the verse that holds nothing for the inner being is standalone. The role comes from this verse, never from the cluster tag. Where a standalone word proves to qualify a characteristic, it is a qualifier of it.

A qualifier gets no separate account of itself, but what it gives the characteristic it binds to is evaluated for its value and recorded as a qualification finding, applied by its nodes to the qualifier (role qualifier) and the characteristic (role characteristic). What it gives can vary widely: grade, nature, impact, size, relation, a measure, strengthening, ground, cause, object, setting or bait are examples, not a list (#2273 D9). A qualifier whose usage varies across contexts may earn its own reading later.
Record how the M-code words work together (a relational observation). Record any pointer outside the verse separately, without resolving it inline.

Record the parties: who bears the act, who causes it, who is acted on (source, target, impact, purpose), and the route (cfg_enum observation_route). A non-human being is never itself a HIB; a collective stays one HIB; an implied party is named as referential, never asserted.
Read the T3 operations, movement and force, negators (a refusal is an act), connectives, body parts, places, objects and nature for what they carry here; read every row, untagged ones too.

For every word that names an inner or bodily act, look at the original: the root's range in all three meaning sources read together, never one picked and the others dropped; the ESV renderings across its verses; whether the English adds or hides; the literal sense beside the rendering. Where more than one reading is open, record each, and mark the choice 'I read'.

Record each relevant word's face as it appears HERE: the circumstance in this verse and where the sense departs from the general gloss. Identifying and clarifying the face is lexical work; what the faces do for the inner being, and a double meaning in different scenarios, are layer 2 of the collection reading (layer-aspects-are-ledgered-and-never-left-open).
Never close a verse or item on 'not X'. A role label is never a verdict; the close records what the verse is. Silence about the inner being is a finding, recorded as data with its reason.
A phenomenon hidden behind a stated or refrained act may be named, with the verb, clause or stated silence that grounds it, and whether it is stated or read.
A literary or structural pattern is not an inner-being observation: log it as an open question instead. A human/divine comparison is recorded only where the text's own wording anchors it.
Keep the source of an interior state apart from the source of an enablement to act.
Morph is read, not carried: where occurrences of a word show different stems or voices, record whether the subject does, undergoes or causes the act.
A difference, or a specific inference, is its own observation, never folded into another.

A word that is only a homonym or a name, with no meaningful context, is recorded as such (tag no-human-context) and left. Data errors found while reading are flagged (tag data-error), not fixed in the reading.
The question catalogue's questions are prompts for the areas to explore. A question that does not apply is not answered, and no answer is manufactured beyond what the verse shows.
Faculty (heart, soul, spirit, mind) is reflected on at the end, over the scope, not per word.
Before reading the whole scope, read a few verses and have them checked.
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.

A reading records findings of eight kinds (cfg_setting reading.observation_parts; the kind is the tag): face, qualification, party, statement, link, use, term, silence. A finding holds its text, meaning, implication, basis, its structured parts (ib_observation.parts: item, and mode, polarity, flag_type or grounds where its item needs them; reading.observation_items) and, on a party or link finding, its route; its nodes hold the verse, the word, the occurrence, the collection and its subgroup, the word's role in the finding and the reading that applied it. The silence kind is not used by Analysis_phase_1: a surface with no inner-being role is not recorded.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
An observation about a word can be answered only by consulting this occurrence's verse, span and morph.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.

A flag raised in reading (needs adjacent context, a pointer) states its reason and what the follow-up must establish, and is carried to an open item, not resolved inline. Can't-resolve is recorded, never guessed (tag could-not-resolve).
Where the evidence points to more than one reading, each is its own observation with its own evidence.
A re-read includes the observations already recorded for the verse, so the reading sees prior findings and builds on them.
Where a verse ends up for a finding is recorded on the node (ib_node.disposition, cfg_enum observation_disposition: told, claim, held, data, context, withdrawn), with its reason or carrier.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

After recording, every observation is read back against the verse for sense. An uncertain one is recorded as uncertain (tag could-not-resolve, or basis read: 'I read'), never asserted. A rule found to be systematically wrong is raised as a config change with the learning, never worked round in the reading.

A word is read per its lettered Strong's code (its grain), never the bare lemma (B:113). The occurrences of a word with several senses are related per grain and never aggregated across grains: related verses are same-grain occurrences.

Content words carry the inner-being impact and are read even when no cluster tags them. Function words (particles, prepositions, conjunctions, suffixes, pronouns) get no observation of their own, except negators and connectives, which are read for what they do (RG-07). A T2 word never stands alone: it is read as the qualifier of what it binds to.

The words in cfg_setting reading.non_characteristic_strongs are never a verse's characteristic: superscription metadata and named external adversaries. They are read as standalone or as qualifiers. The list is per word, not per cluster, because a cluster can hold both kinds.

A tagged word that works adverbially in an occurrence (a noun with a preposition qualifying the predicate, as 'in the counsel of the wicked') is a qualifier there, not the verse's characteristic. The role is per occurrence: the same word may be the characteristic elsewhere.
In a simile, the predicates of the vehicle (the tree that yields, does not wither) are read for what they say of the one compared (the tenor), not as the vehicle's own acts.

An existing observation counts for a surface when its node names that occurrence (verse_lexical_id), or, with none, when the node's verse, Strong and surface match one occurrence only. A node that names a verse and no surface, or matches more than one occurrence, is set aside: it does not count for any surface.

When a verse is worked, every existing observation and node on it, of any stage, is checked against the verse by its wording. The stage is not an indication of the nature of an observation and is never used to filter. Each observation is accepted, modified (changed in place; the old value, the new value and the reason are kept in ib_observation_change), soft deleted (the `deleted` column, with the reason), merged (a duplicate description, into the observation that is kept) or, when its wording shows it is not verse understanding, left exactly as it is with the reason. The check's fixes are part of it and need no separate approval. Nothing is physically deleted.

A surface with no inner-being role in a verse has no observation of its own. A word read in the verse that holds nothing for the inner being has the role standalone, which is a role and not an absence; where it could be a qualifier it is read as the qualifier of the characteristic it serves.

The observations of a verse state what the verse shows, and Record enforces it from cfg_setting reading.observation_rules and reading.observation_items: an observation of a relevant surface carries parts.item (one of the nine items), is written as one of the kinds that item allows, on a basis the item allows (a read observation names its grounds), and carries what its item needs (polarity, mode, flag type; a party carries its route). The words that bear on an act are nodes of the observation of the act, never an observation of their own (bears_on_only_refused). Every surface with the role characteristic has each applicable item observed or stated absent with the reason; the verse always has an operation observation. A verse whose observations do not comply is not recorded (#2329).

For every surface with the role characteristic, the nine items of spec 4.2 (reading.observation_items) are each explored, and each applicable item is its own observation (parts.item), written once and applied to every characteristic it is true of by its nodes; a qualifier or shared observation carries nodes on every characteristic it covers. An item the verse does not show gets no observation and is stated absent on the surface (items_absent) with the reason; the meaning item is never absent. The operation item carries a mode (done, foreseen, commanded, negated, reported) and an action description of who or what does what, read from before and after as the verse itself states them (passage-level before and after are the claims process's); the verse always has an operation observation. A read observation (basis read) names its grounds in the words of the verse (parts.grounds). No observation restates the verse text (no run of more than reading.observation_items max_verse_words_copied words). The same text for all items is not an exploration of them. Which word is the characteristic is the verse's decision, never the cluster's (RG-03). The nuance pointers (reading.nuance_pointers) say where each nuance is recorded (#2329).

rows.asks: What do the stage 3 observations of this subgroup (its definition, its Strong's enrichment, its pairings, qualifiers, entities, direction, relations and double meanings, with the stage 1 senses) show of the elements of a behaviour of the inner being: what is done and its mode, whether a refusal or a pursuit, what it is directed at, the outward act, the other party with the route, the circumstance, the chain of operations, and the dimensions of the working (what a qualifier or a variation of the word gives it, from the lexical variation the stage 3 observations record)? Each finding is one observation that rests on named observations (a traced node on each) and carries nodes on the occurrences those observations cover, with the role each has; an occurrence outside them is allowed only with a read-back (the verse and why). Every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on by a finding or declared not used, with the reason. A finding is a building block and never a claim about the behaviour as a whole (stage 5).

interventions: Work from the observations: the stage 3 observations of the subgroup are the input, and the verses are base data read back only where an observation does not settle the point; a read-back is recorded (the verse and why).
Read the lexical variation (the different Strong's codes of a surface, the forms of a word, the double meanings) as the dimensions of how the working happens, not as a difference to be smoothed away.
A behaviour is discovered from the elements, not assumed from the subgroup: a subgroup may form one behaviour, part of one, join others, or form none.

Record building blocks only. A statement of what a behaviour is, is a claim and belongs to stage 5; stage 5 receives the observations and not the subgroups, so everything it will need from them is recorded here.
Check the original where an observation depends on the word's range (RG-08); do not force a meaning and never close on 'not X' (RG-10).

A word whose role is not its collection's is reclassified by the collection change procedure and the step reopens (B:129, B:134); a discovery outside the observations is recorded as a flag finding of type discovery and is not resolved inline (RW-07).

may_rest_on_besides.text: In 2Cor 5:16 the perfect verb 'to know' has Christ as object and the phrase 'according to the flesh' as its standard: the sense is to have known and sized up in that way, a settled judgment of him; the ESV renders it regard. The pick-up note on this word is checked against the verse and stands.

In Luk 22:24 the verb 'to think' stands in a clause about which of the disciples is to be regarded as greatest: it is the standing assigned to a person, 'to be reckoned', and not what the subject thinks.

In Rom 2:26 and Rom 8:36 the verb 'to reckon' is passive and carries an 'as': the uncircumcised will be counted as circumcision, and the believers are counted as sheep for slaughter; the sense is 'to be counted as', a status assigned.

In Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Lam 4:2 and Hos 8:12 the Niphal perfect of the verb 'to reckon' is followed by 'as' and the thing compared: foreigners, sheep to be slaughtered, earthen pots, a strange thing; the sense is 'to be accounted as', the status others give.

In Isa 29:16 and Isa 29:17 the Niphal imperfect of the verb 'to reckon' is in two questions with 'as' and the thing compared (the potter as clay; the fruitful field as a forest); the sense is 'to be counted as', a status turned upside down.

In 2Cor 5:16 the present verb 'to know' with 'thus' no longer is the second half of the verse's contrast with the earlier regarding of Christ; the sense is to know or size up, now ended as a way of knowing him.

In 2Th 3:15 and 1Ti 6:1 the present imperative of the verb 'to lead, count' has an 'as' complement: do not count him as an enemy, let bondservants count their masters as worthy of honor; the sense is 'to esteem as', a judgment of status.

In 1Cor 4:1 and 1Pe 5:12 the verb 'to reckon' has a person as object and an 'as' complement: in 1Cor 4:1 how the apostles are to be taken, as servants and stewards, and in 1Pe 5:12 Peter's estimate of Silvanus as a faithful brother; the sense is 'to consider as'.

In Col 2:16 the noun 'part, share' stands in a prepositional idiom ('in a part of') that introduces the topics of food, drink, festival, new moon and Sabbath; it means 'with regard to' and is not a thinking word, which departs from the dictionary sense 'part'.

In 2Cor 5:16 the perfect verb 'to know' has 'no one' as object and 'according to the flesh' as its standard; the lexicon lists 'to have regard for one, to pay attention to' for the code, and the verse sets it before the later regard for Christ.

In Exo 5:9 the negative 'not' (used with a verb: let not) stands in the jussive and bears on the regarding of lying words (H8159 in the same verse): the work is to be heavier so that the men do not pay heed; the verse states its reach.

In Psa 28:5 the Qal imperfect of the verb 'to discern' is negated and has the works of the Lord as object: they do not discern or give heed to them; the sense is attentive understanding, which the verse says is lacking in the wicked.

In Ecc 3:18 the noun 'cause, manner' stands in an idiom that opens 'I said in my heart': it means 'with regard to' the children of man and is a prepositional use, not a word of thought; it departs from the dictionary sense 'cause'.

In Isa 13:17 and Isa 33:8 the Qal of the verb 'to reckon' is negated and has silver and man as objects: the Medes have no regard for silver, there is no regard for man; the sense is 'to esteem, value', the lexicon's 'to esteem, value, regard'.

In Job 9:21, Psa 144:3 and Pro 12:10 the verb 'to know' means to take knowing account of someone with care: the speaker does not regard himself, the Lord regards man, and the righteous regards the life of his beast; the sense is 'to take note of, acknowledge'.
In Job 9:21 the negative 'not' follows 'I regard' (H3045 in the same verse) and bears on it: the verse states that he does not regard himself; the reach is the verb of regarding.

In 1Sa 25:25 the noun 'heart' is not the speaker's word for a faculty but the object-word of an idiom of setting the heart on someone, in the plea that the lord not take Nabal to heart; the ESV renders it 'regard', and the unit is shared with the verb.

In Psa 74:20, Isa 5:12 and Lam 4:16 the Hiphil of the verb 'to look' means to look upon with regard: in Psa 74:20 the covenant is the object the Lord is asked to look to, in Isa 5:12 the feasters give no heed to what the Lord has done, in Lam 4:16 the Lord's looking on them is withdrawn; it includes both attention and favour.

In Jer 24:5 the Hiphil of the verb 'to recognize' has the exiles as object and 'as good' as complement: the Lord will recognise and regard them as good; the sense is 'to acknowledge, regard', as the lexicon lists the Hiphil.

In 2Ki 3:14 the verb 'to lift' is part of the idiom 'to lift the face of someone', the sense given by the lexicon head 'favour, honour': Elisha says he has regard for Jehoshaphat, which is why he acts; it is respect shown, not lifting.

In 1Sa 1:16 the verb 'to give, put' stands in a plea not to be set as a worthless woman: the speaker asks not to be reckoned as one; the verb of giving is used of reckoning, which departs from its first sense.

In Lev 19:23 the verb 'to count uncircumcised' is a denominative of the foreskin: the fruit of a newly planted tree is to be counted as uncircumcised, which the verse spells out as forbidden for three years; the sense is 'to treat as foreskin, withheld'.

In Deu 9:27 and 2Ch 6:19 the verb 'to turn' is used with a prepositional object of what the Lord is asked to turn toward or not to turn toward: do not regard the stubbornness, have regard to the prayer; it is attention directed, not a physical turning.

In Psa 80:14 the Qal imperative 'visit' follows 'look down from heaven, and see' and has the vine as object: the sense is to attend to and care for, which the lexicon lists for the code (to attend to, look after, care for).

In Deu 33:9 and Job 37:24 the verb 'to see' is negated: in Deu 33:9 the Levite's words of his parents, in Job 37:24 God's attitude to the self-wise; the sense is to look upon with regard, which the lexicon lists, here withheld.
In Job 35:13 the verb 'to behold' is negated and has the empty cry as object: the Almighty does not look upon it; the sense is to take notice of, the lexicon's 'to regard'.

In Job 34:27 the Hiphil perfect of the verb 'to be prudent' is negated and has all his ways as object: they had no regard for them; the sense is 'to give heed to, consider', which the lexicon lists for the Hiphil.

In 2Ch 5:11 the verb 'to keep, observe' is in a phrase about the priests being present without regard to their divisions; the sense is not keeping to the order of their courses, observing a rule, which the ESV gives as 'regard'.

In Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9 and Psa 119:117 the verb 'to gaze at' is used of regard, with its object a person's offering, lying words and the Lord's statutes: Cain's offering was not looked on, the men are not to look to lying words, the psalmist asks to look continually at the statutes.

Included with: γιγνώσκω,
Doric dialect [Refs 5th c.BC+], Aeolic dialect, Ionic dialect, and after [Refs 4th c.BC+] γινώσκω, but γιγνώσκω in early Attic dialect Inscrr., as [Refs] (κατα-), etc.: future γνώσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+], Doric dialect 3rd.pers. singular γνωσεῖται [Refs] is false reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+]; Cretan dialect form ἀνα-γνώοντι uncertain in [Refs]: perfect ἔγνωκα [Refs 5th c.BC+]: aorist 2 ἔγνων [Refs 8th c.BC+], Epic dialect dual γνώτην [Refs 8th c.BC+], Doric dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἔγνον [Refs 5th c.BC+]; subjunctive γνῶ, γνῷς, γνῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+], Epic dialect also γνώω, γνώομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; infinitive γνῶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+], Epic dialect γνώμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+]; participle γνούς [Refs 5th c.BC+]:—middle, aorist 1 γνώσασθαι [Refs 4th c.AD+]:—passive, future γνωσθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]: aorist ἐγνώσθην [Refs 5th c.BC+]: perfect ἔγνωσμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]:— come to know, perceive, and in past tenses, know, with accusative, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; as distinct from οἶδα know by reflection, γιγνώσκω, = know by observation, γνόντες δὲ εἰδότας περιορᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; χαλεπόν ἐστι τὸ γνῶναι εἰ οἶδεν ἢ μή it is hard to perceive whether one knows or not, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; discern, distinguish, recognize, ὄφρ᾽ εὖ γιγνώσκῃς ἠμὲν θεὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἄνδρα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ironically, εὖ νύ τις αὐτὸν γνώσεται he will learn him to his cost,[Refs 3rd c.BC+] were aware of.., [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__2 followed by relative clauses, γιγνώσκω δ᾽ ὡς.. I perceive that..,[Refs 8th c.BC+]; γ. ὅτι.. [Refs 4th c.BC+]; ἵν᾽ εἰδῆτε ὑμεῖς καὶ γνῶτε ὅτι.. [Refs 8th c.BC+]; τοὺς Πέρσας γ. ὅτι.. [Refs]participle, ἔγνων μιν.. οἰωνὸν ἐόντα perceived that he was.., [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἔγνων ἡττημένος I felt that I was beaten, [Refs 5th c.BC+] when he was aware of.., [Refs 8th c.BC+]: with infinitive, ἵνα γνῷ τρέφειν τὴν γλῶσσαν ἡσυχεστέραν [Refs 5th c.BC+]: with accusative et infinitive, recognize that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; take a thing to mean that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]: with double accusative, perceive or know another to be.., οἵους γνώσεσθε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους [Refs 5th c.BC+] the perceiver, opposed to τὰ γιγνωσκόμενα the objects perceived, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also ὁ γ. one who knows, a prudent person, [Refs]:—passive, εἰ γνωσθεῖεν ᾧ.. if it were known of them in what.., [Refs]
__II form a judgement, think, ταὐτά [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἃ γιγνώσκω λέγειν (={τὴν γνώμην λ}.) [Refs 4th c.BC+]; τοῦτο γιγνώσκων, ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+] see thou to that, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; especially in dialogue, ἔγνων I understand, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔγνως you are right, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔγνωκα; Latin tenes? [Refs 4th c.BC+]; judge, determine, decree that.., with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: with infinitive, determine to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]:— passive, to be pronounced, of a sentence or judgement, [Refs 5th c.BC+]

lexicon.lsj:
δοκέω
[Refs 8th c.BC+]imperfect ἐδόκουν, Epic dialect δοκέεσκον [Refs 6th c.AD+]: —middle, δοκέοντο [Refs 3rd c.AD+]: participle δοκεύμενος[Refs]: the future and other tenses are twofold:
__1 future δόξω and aorist 1 ἔδοξα [Refs 5th c.BC+]perfect δέδοχα inferred from pluperfect ἐδεδόχεσαν [Refs 2nd c.AD+]:—passive, aorist ἐδόχθην [Refs 5th c.BC+]: perfect δέδογμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]: pluperfect ἐδέδοκτο [Refs]
__2 regular forms (chiefly Trag., Comedy texts, and late Prose), future δοκήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+]; Doric dialect δοκησῶ or -ᾱσῶ[Refs 3rd c.BC+]aorist ἐδόκησα, Epic dialect δόκ- [Refs 8th c.BC+]: perfect δεδόκηκα [Refs 4th c.BC+]:— passive, aorist ἐδοκήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+]: perfect δεδόκημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+].; but δεδοκημένος (which see) belongs to δέχομαι.
__I expect (Iterat. of δέκομαι,[Refs]: hence, think, suppose, imagine, (opposed to φρονέω, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__I.1 with accusative et infinitive, δοκέω νικησέμεν Ἕκτορα [Refs 8th c.BC+]infinitive omitted, δοκῶ.. οὐδὲν ῥῆμα.. κακὸν [εἶναι] [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τούτους τι δοκεῖτε [εἶναι] [Refs 5th c.BC+]; frequently in relating a dream or vision, τεκεῖν δράκοντ᾽ ἔδοξεν she thought a serpent produced young, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; ἐδόκουν αἰετὸν.. φέρειν methought an eagle was carrying, [Refs 5th c.BC+]infinitive only, ἔδοξ᾽ ἰδεῖν methought I saw,[Refs 5th c.BC+] (sometimes also, as in signification [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__I.1.b think to do, purpose, ὅταν δ᾽ ἀείδειν.. δοκῶ [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__I.2 absolutely, have or form an opinion, περί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+]; mostly in parenthetic phrases, ὡς δοκῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+]; δοκῶ alone, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; πῶς δοκεῖ; to call attention to something remarked, τοῦτον, πῶς δοκεῖ; καθύβρισεν [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__I.3 δοκῶ μοι I seem to myself, methinks, with infinitive, ἐγώ μοι δοκέω κατανοέειν τοῦτο [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οὔ μοι δοκῶ I think not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; δοκῶ μοι parenthetic, [Refs]
__I.3.b δοκῶ μοι I am determined, resolved, with infinitive present, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: with infinitive future, [Refs 4th c.BC+]: with infinitive aorist, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+]: rarely without μοι, think fit, σὺ δ᾽ αὐτὸς ἤδη γνῶθι τίνα πέμπειν δοκεῖς [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__I.4 seem, pretend, with infinitive (with or without negative), ὁρέων μὲν οὐδέν, δοκέων δὲ [ὁρᾶν] uncertain reading in [Refs 7th c.BC+]
__I.5 passive, to be considered, δοκεῖσθαι οὕτω [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ νῦν δοκούμενα περί τινος the current opinions, [Refs]
__I.6 middle, [Refs 3rd c.AD+]
__II of an Object, seem, with dative person et infinitive present, δοκέεις δέ μοι οὐκ ἀπινύσσειν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; δόκησε δ᾽ ἄρα σφίσι θυμὸς ὣς ἔμεν ὡς εἰ.. their heart seemed just as if.., felt as though.., [Refs]infinitive future, seem likely, δοκέει δέ μοι ὧδε λώϊον ἔσσεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+]: with infinitive aorist (never in [Refs 8th c.BC+]; seem or be thought to have done, especially of suspected persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; to be convicted, ἂν ἁλῷ καὶ δοκῇ τοὔργον εἰργάσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__II.2 absolutely, seem, as opposed to to reality, τὸ δοκεῖν καὶ τὰν ἀλάθειαν βιᾶται [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.3 seem good, be resolved on, εἰ δοκεῖ σοι ταῦτα[Refs]
__II.4 frequently impersonal, δοκεῖ μοι it seems to me, methinks, ὥς μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι ἄριστα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκεῖ as I think, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; τὸ σοὶ δοκοῦν your opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+]infinitive in parenthesis clause, ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκέειν to my thinking, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; without μοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.4.b it seems good to me, it is my pleasure, δοκεῖ ἡμῖν χρῆσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]: frequently of a public resolution, τοῖσι Ἕλλησι δόξαι.. ἀπαιτέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; especially in decrees and the like, ἔδοξε τῇ βουλῇ, τῷ δήμῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+]:—passive, δέδοκται [Refs 5th c.BC+] when it was decreed or resolved, δόξαν αὐτοῖς ὥστε διαναυμαχεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; δόξαν δέ σφι (i.e. λιπέσθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἰδίᾳ δοκῆσάν σοι τόδ᾽..; [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.5 to be reputed, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; δοκοῦντες εἶναί τι men who are held to be something, men of repute, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ δοκοῦντα, opposed to τὰ μηδὲν ὄντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; to be an established, current opinion, [Refs 4th c.BC+] — passive, οἱ δεδογμένοι ἀνδροφόνοι those who have been found guilty of homicide, [Refs 4th c.BC+] that which seems true is true to him who thinks it, [Refs 5th c.BC+]

lexicon.lsj:
ἡγέομαι,
Doric dialect ἁγ- (irregular present participle ἁγώμενος [Refs]imperfect ἡγούμην[Refs], Ionic dialect -εύμην[Refs 5th c.BC+]: future ἡγήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+]: aorist 1 ἡγησάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+]aorist 1 ἡγήθην[Refs 3rd c.AD+]: perfect ἥγημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]:—go before, lead the way, ὣς εἰπὼν ἡγεῖθ᾽, ἡ δ᾽ ἕσπετο Παλλὰς 'Αθήνη [Refs 8th c.BC+]: Astron., precede in the daily movement, [Refs 4th c.BC+]

__d with accusative loci, ἥ οἱ.. πόλιν ἡγήσαιτο who might guide him to the city, [Refs 8th c.BC+]

lexicon.lsj:
λογ-ίζομαι,
Attic dialect future -ιοῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]: aorist ἐλογισάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+]: perfect λελόγισμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]:—passive, see below 111: (λόγος):—properly of numerical calculation, count, reckon, οὐκ ἐπισταμένους λογίζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+]; in full, λ. ψήφοισι [Refs]; λόγισαι φαύλως, μὴ ψήφοις ἀλλ᾽ ἀπὸ χειρός calculate roughly, not by rule, but off-hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+] with accusative _of things_, λ. τοὺς τόκους calculate the interest, [Refs] minae and set down[Refs]
__2 with accusative et infinitive, reckon or calculate that.., λ. μύρια εἶναι [τὰ ἔτεα] [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__3 λ. τινί τι set down to one's account, οὗτος.. τὸ ἥμισυ τούτοις.. λελόγισται [Refs 5th c.BC+], compare 27; τἀνηλωμέν᾽.. οὐκ ἐλογιζόμην I did not charge them.., [NT+4th c.BC+]
__3.b audit the accounts of a person, with dative, τοῖς ὑπευθύνοις [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__II without reference to numbers, take into account, calculate, consider, ταῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+]; λ. τι πρός τινας with them, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; also λ. περί τινος calculate, form calculations about.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.2 with accusative et infinitive, reckon, consider that.., τὸν ἕτερον [παῖδα] οὐκ εἶναί μοι λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+]; λ. ὅτι.. or ὡς.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐλογιζόμην πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν.., ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+]: with accusative et participle, Σμέρδιν μηκέτι ὑμῖν ἐόντα λογίζεσθε [Refs 5th c.BC+]: also with infinitive omitted, reckon or account so and so, τὸν καθ᾽ ἡμέραν βίον λογίζου σόν [εἶναι], τὰ δ᾽ ἄλλα τῆς τύχης [Refs 5th c.BC+]; πολὺν [εἶναι] τὸν κάτω χρόνον[Refs 5th c.BC+]; μίαν ἄμφω τούτω τὼ ἡμέρα λ. count both days as one, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.3 with infinitive also, count or reckon upon doing, calculate or expect that.., ἐπισιτιεῖσθαι ἐλογίζοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τί λογίζομ᾽.. προσδοκῶν χάριν παρὰ γυναικὸς κομιεῖσθα; [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__II.4 count upon, εἴ τις δύο ἢ καί τι πλείους ἡμέρας λ., μάταιός ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.5 conclude by reasoning, infer that.., with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; λ. ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__II.6 absolutely, τοὺς ἐπισταμένους λογίζεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+]; ὁ σπουδαῖος λελόγισται ἤδη has finished reasoning, [Refs 3rd c.AD+]
__III passive, mostly aorist ἐλογίσθην and (less frequently) perfect λελόγισμαι, also in present, participle λογιζόμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+], frequently in later Gr., [NT+3rd c.BC+]; χρήματα εἰς ἀργύριον λογισθέντα counted or calculated in silver, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸ λελογισμένον, ={λογισμός}, [Refs 5th c.BC+]

lexicon.lsj:
περί,
Thess., Delph. περ [Refs 5th c.BC+], also Aeolic dialect, see below [Refs 4th c.BC+] V; Elean παρ [Refs]: preposition with genitive, dative, and accusative:—round about, all round (properly different from ἀμφί, on both sides). (Cogn. with Sanskrit pári 'round about'.)
__A WITH GENITIVE,
__A.I of Place, sometimes in Poets, round about, around, τετάνυστο π. σπείους ἡμερίς [Refs 8th c.BC+], on both sides, see at {περιβαίνω} [Refs]
__A.I.2 about near, π. σοῦ πάντα γένοιτο ῥόδα [Refs]
__A.II to denote the object about or for which one does something:
__A.II.1 with Verbs of fighting or contending, π. τινός for an object—from the notion of the thing's lying in the middle to be fought about, π. τῶνδε for these prizes, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; δόλους καὶ μῆτιν ὕφαινον, ὥς τε π. ψυχῆς since it was for my life, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; in Prose, τρέχειν π. ἑωυτοῦ, π. τῆς ψυχῆς, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; and without a Verb, π. γῆς ὅρων διαφοραί [Refs 8th c.BC+]; but ἐρίσσαι π. μύθων contend about speaking, i. e. who can speak best, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.II.2 with words which denote care or anxiety, about, on account of, π. Τρώων.. μερμηρίζειν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; κρίνειν, διαγιγνώσκειν π. τ., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. τ. ψηφίζεσθαι, διαψηφίζεσθαι, ψῆφον φέρειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; διανοεῖσθαι, σκοπεῖν π. τινός, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. πότου γοῦν ἐστί σο; so with you it is a question of drink? [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.II.3 with Verbs of hearing, knowing, speaking, etc., about, concerning, π. νόστου ἄκουσα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; π. τινὸς ἐρέειν, λέγειν, λόγον ποιήσασθαι, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. τινὸς ἀγγεῖλαι, κηρῦξαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. τινὸς διελθεῖν, διεξελθεῖν, διηγεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.II.4 of impulse or motive rather than object, ἐμαρνάσθην ἔριδος πέρι fought for very enmity, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.II.5 about, in regard to, μεμηνυμένος π. τινός [Refs 5th c.BC+]: in Prose frequently without a Verb, ἡ π. τῶν Μαντινικῶν πρᾶξις [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ π. τινός the circumstances of.., [Refs]; οὕτω δὴ καὶ π. τῶν ἀρετῶν (i.e. ἔχει) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. τοῦ καταλειφθῆναι τὸν σῖτον as for reserving the corn, [Refs 3rd c.BC+] as to number, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; χρηστηρίων δὲ πέρι.. [Refs]
__A.III before, above, beyond, of superiority, chiefly in Epic dialect, π. πάντων ἔμμεναι ἄλλων [Refs 8th c.BC+] in understanding to be beyond them, [Refs 8th c.BC+] —In this sense π. is sometimes adverbial, and the genitive is absent, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.IV in [Refs 5th c.BC+] it is of much consequence, worth much, to us, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. πολλοῦ ποιεῖσθαί τινας to reckon them for, i.e. worth, much, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. πλείονος, π. πλείστου ποιεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. ἐλάττονος ἡγούμενοι, π. οὐδενὸς ἡγήσασθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.V Aeolic dialect περί and περ ={ὑπέρ, στροῦθοι περὶ γᾶς.. δίννεντες πτέρα} [Refs 7th c.BC+]; περ κεφάλας probably in [Refs 7th c.BC+]; also Hellenistic, ὃ διέγραψε Προῖτος περί μου paid on my behalf, PCair. Zen.[Refs 3rd c.BC+]
__B WITH DATIVE (in Attic dialect Prose mostly in signification [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I of Place, round about, around, of close-fitting dresses, armour, etc., ἔνδυνε π. στήθεσσι χιτῶνα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; οἱ στρεπτοὶ οἱ π. τῇ δέρῃ καὶ τὰ ψέλια π. ταῖς χερσί[Refs 8th c.BC+]; in other relations, π. δ᾽ ἔγχεϊ χεῖρα καμεῖται will grow weary by grasping the spear,[Refs]: rarely in Trag., π. βρέτει πλεχθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.2 in Poets, also, around a weapon, i. e. spitted upon it, transfixed by it, π. δουρὶ πεπαρμένη [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__B.I.3 of a warrior standing over a dead comrade so as to defend him, ἀμφὶ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ αὐτῷ βαῖν᾽, ὥς τις π. πόρτακι μήτηρ [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.II of an object for or about which one struggles (compare above [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__B.II.2 with Verbs denoting care, anxiety, or the opposite (compare above [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__B.II.3 generally, of the cause or occasion, on account of, by reason of, ἀτύζεσθαι π. καπνῷ, variant for{ὑπὸ καπνοῦ} in [Refs 8th c.BC+] for fear, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. τιμᾷ in honour or praise, [Refs]; π. τάρβει, π. φόβῳ, [Refs 4th c.BC+] —but π. θυμῷ is false reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__C WITH ACCUSATIVE,
__C.I of Place, properly of the object round about which motion takes place, π. βόθρον ἐφοίτων came flocking round the pit, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐρύσας π. σῆμα [Refs 8th c.BC+]: also of extension round, ἑστάμεναι π. τοῖχον, π. βωμόν, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; π. τὴν κρήνην εὕδειν somewhere near it, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. λίθον πεσών upon it, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. αὑτὰ καταρρεῖν collapse upon themselves, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; πλεῦνες π. ἕνα many to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. τὸν ἄρξαντα.. τὸ ἀδίκημά ἐστι is imputable to him who.., [Refs 5th c.BC+] substantive only, ἡ π. Λέσβον ναυμαχία the sea-fight off Lesbos, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__C.I.2 of persons who are about one, ἔχειν τινὰ π. αὑτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; especially οἱ π. τινά a person's attendants, connexions, associates, or colleagues, οἱ π. τὸν Πείσανδρον πρέσβεις [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ π. Ἡράκλειτον his school, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ π. Ἀρχίαν πολέμαρχοι Archias and his colleagues, [Refs]; οἱ π. τινά so-and-so and his family, [Refs 2nd c.BC+]; later οἱ π. τινά, periphrastic for the person himself, οἱ π. Φαβρίκιον Fabricius, [Refs 1st c.AD+]; compare ἀμφί C. 1.3.
__C.I.3 of the object about which one is occupied or concerned, π. δόρπα πονεῖσθαι, π. δεῖπνον πένεσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; later mostly εἶναι π. τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. γυναῖκας γενέσθαι Vett.[Refs 5th c.BC+]; in periphrastic phrases, οἱ π. τὴν ποίησιν καὶ τοὺς λόγους ὄντες poets and orators, [Refs 5th c.BC+] ministers of the mysteries, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὁ π. τὸν ἵππον the groom, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__C.I.4 round or about a place, and so in, π. νῆσον ἀλώμενοι [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἃν π. ψυχὰν γάθησεν in his heart, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ π. Φωκίδα τόποι [Refs 2nd c.BC+]
__C.I.5 about, in the case of, τὰ π. τὴν Αἴγυπτον γεγονότα, τὰ π. Μίλητον γενόμενα, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ποιέειν or πράττειν τι π. τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; σπουδάζειν π. τινά promote his cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: without a Verb, αἱ π. τοὺς παῖδας συμφοραί [Refs 5th c.BC+]: generally, of all relations, about, concerning, in respect of, π. μὲν τοὺς ἰχθύας οὕτως ἔχει [Refs 5th c.BC+]; as to [Refs 5th c.BC+] adjective, ὄργανα ὅσα π. γεωργίαν, i.e. γεωργικά[Refs]; also in place of a genitive, οἱ π. Αυσίαν λόγοι the speeches of L., [Refs]; ἡ π. Φίλιππον τυραννίς the despotism of P., [Refs 5th c.BC+]: in Prose, to denote circumstances connected with any person or thing, τὰ π. Κῦρον, τὰ π. Ἑλένην, τὰ π. Βάττον, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ π. τὸν Ἄθων the works at Mount Athos, [Refs]; τὰ π. τὰς ναῦς naval affairs, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ π. τὴν ναυμαχίαν (variant for{τῆς ναυμαχίας}) the events of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__C.II of Time, π. λύχνων ἁφάς about the time of lamp-lighting, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. μέσας νύκτας about midnight, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; π. ἡλίου δυσμάς[Refs 5th c.BC+]
__C.II.2 of round numbers, π. ἑβδομήκοντα about seventy, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__D Position: π. may follow its substantive, when it suffers anastrophe, ἄστυ πέρι [Refs 8th c.BC+] only once uses it before its genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__E περί absolutely, as adverb., around, about, also, near, by, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+]round about, [Refs 3rd c.BC+]
__E.II before or above others [Refs 4th c.BC+], exceedingly, only Epic dialect, in which case it commonly suffers anastrophe, Τυδεΐδη, πέρι μέν σε τίον Δαναοί [Refs 8th c.BC+]; σε χρὴ πέρι μὲν φάσθαι ἔπος ἠδ᾽ ἐπακοῦσαι[Refs 8th c.BC+]
__E.II.2 π. does not suffer anastrophe in the Epic dialect phrase π. κῆρι right heartily, π. κῆρι φίλησε [Refs 8th c.BC+]; π. κῆρι τιέσκετο[Refs 8th c.BC+]
__E.II.3 for περὶ πρό, see at {περιπρό}.
__E.II.4 περὶ κάτω bottom upwards, δῖνος π. κάτω τετραμμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__F IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words), all its chief senses recur, especially
__F.I extension in all directions as from a centre, all round, as in περιβάλλω, περιβλέπω, περιέχω.
__F.II completion of an orbit and return to the same point, about, as in περιάγω, περιβαίνω, περίειμι (εἶμι ibo), περιέρχομαι, περιστρέφω.
__F.III a going over or beyond, above, before, as in περιβαίνω III, περιβάλλω see, περιγίγνομαι, περιεργάζομαι, περιτοξεύω.
__F.IV generally, a strengthening of the simple notion, beyond measure, very, exceedingly, as in περικαλλής, περίκηλος, περιδείδω, like Latin per-.
__F.V the notion of double-ness which belongs to ἀμφί is found in only one poetic compound, περιδέξιος (which see).
__G PROSODY: περί never suffers elision in [Refs 8th c.BC+] near the end; περ᾽ ἰγνύῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+]; in Comedy texts and codices of Prose writers only in participle of περίειμι (εἶμι ibo) (which see):—π. stands before a word beginning with a vowel in Comedy texts, περὶ Ἀθηνῶν, περὶ ἐμοῦ, [Refs 5th c.BC+] {περιαγαπάζομαι}:—Aeolic dialect περρ for the sake of meter, see [Refs 4th c.BC+]

findings.text: Regard is given as a done act in 2Ki 3:14 (Elisha has regard for Jehoshaphat), Pro 12:10 (the righteous man's care for his beast), Psa 144:3 (the Lord regards man) and 2Cor 5:16 (Christ once regarded according to the flesh). The act is a taking account of a person or a creature, and the subjects are a prophet, a righteous man, the Lord and the apostles.

Regard and its counting-as are foreseen in Jer 24:5 (the Lord will regard the exiles as good), Isa 29:17 (the fruitful field shall be counted as a forest) and Rom 2:26 (the uncircumcised will be counted as circumcision). The act stands in the future and gives a standing that does not yet hold.

Regard is asked or commanded in Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14 and 2Ch 6:19 (that the Lord have regard for the covenant, the vine and the prayer) and in 1Ti 6:1 and 1Cor 4:1 (that bondservants regard their masters as worthy, that the apostles be taken as servants). The act is put as what should be done, by God in the first three and by persons in the last two.

Regard is negated in thirteen verses: Gen 4:5, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 25:25, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16, 2Th 3:15 and Exo 5:9. The negator reaches the member in each (no regard, do not regard, nor does he regard), and the subjects are Cain's rival, the Levite, a lord, the wicked, God and the feasters, so the denial runs both from persons and from God.

In these thirteen verses the act is a refusal as the grammar states it: the regard is withheld from an offering, a person, the Lord's works, silver, man or a prayer. The refusal is spoken of God in Gen 4:5, Job 35:13, Job 37:24 and Lam 4:16, and of persons in the others.

Where regard is given or asked, the act is a pursuit of its object: the Lord is asked to look to the covenant, the vine and the prayer, Elisha acts out of regard for Jehoshaphat, and the righteous cares for his beast. The pursuit runs from persons to God's works and to persons, and from God to persons.

What the regard is directed at differs by verse: the Lord's works and deeds (Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12), the covenant, the vine and the prayer (Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14, 2Ch 6:19), persons (Nabal in 1Sa 25:25, Jehoshaphat in 2Ki 3:14, the exiles in Jer 24:5, the parents in Deu 33:9), Cain's offering (Gen 4:5), an empty cry (Job 35:13) and the self-wise (Job 37:24). Persons and the works of God are the commonest objects.

After 'regarded' and 'regard' the complement gives the standing: foreigners (Gen 31:15), a strange thing (Hos 8:12), the greatest (Luk 22:24), worthy of honor (1Ti 6:1). Each complement is a qualifier of the counting or regarding, naming what the person or thing is counted as.

The negator is a qualifier of the regard it reaches, turning the act into a denial: 'no' in Gen 4:5, 'not' in Job 37:24 and Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12, 'no' in Isa 13:17 and Isa 33:8 and Lam 4:16. In each verse the negator is 1 word before or after the member and the verse states what it reaches.

Regard is bound up with worth in three verses: it is asked not to be given to a woman or a man as worthless (1Sa 1:16, 1Sa 25:25) and God does not give it to those wise in their own conceit (Job 37:24). The worth or the conceit of the person regarded is named in the same sentence, within three words of the member.

A word of contempt stands in the same sentence as the regard in Isa 33:8 (despised, 2 before), Act 28:22 (spoken against, 9 after) and 1Ti 6:1 (reviled, 11 after). The regard is set in a verse that also names the low standing of a city, a sect or a name.

Hearing and regard are paired in 2Ch 6:19 (listening, 8 after), Job 35:13 (hear, 4 before) and Act 28:22 (hear, 6 before): the regard is asked or denied together with a hearing, of a prayer, an empty cry or the views of a sect.

The surface 'regard' also holds the prepositional idiom 'with regard to' in Act 28:22 (G4012), Col 2:16 (G3313), Ecc 3:18 (H1700) and Jdg 15:3 (H9006): these are not an act of taking account of anyone and are read in their verses as standalone. The negators H0408 and H3808 in Exo 5:9 and Job 9:21 are aligned into the unit of the surface and are read as negators, not as acts of regard.
